content: Omeprazole is a medication used to treat conditions caused by excessive stomach acid production. These include heartburn, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), ulcers, and erosive esophagitis. It is also used to manage Helicobacter pylori infections and other conditions where the stomach produces too much acid. Omeprazole works by reducing the amount of acid produced in the stomach. Omeprazole is available under brand names such as Prilosec and Prilosec OTC, as well as in generic forms. It comes in various dosage forms, including capsules, tablets, and packets of powder for delayed-release oral suspension. It should be stored at room temperature (68°F to 77°F or 20°C to 25°C) and kept in a cool, dry place. When taking omeprazole, it is important to follow your healthcare provider's instructions. The medication should be taken before meals, and antacids may be used alongside it if needed. If swallowing capsules is difficult, the contents can be sprinkled on a tablespoon of applesauce and consumed immediately. Omeprazole is not intended for immediate relief of heartburn and may take 1 to 4 days to fully work. Common side effects of omeprazole include headache, stomach pain, nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, gas, and, in children aged 1 to 16 years, infections in the nose or throat and fever. If these side effects bother you, inform your healthcare provider. Serious side effects, though less common, include kidney problems (such as acute tubulointerstitial nephritis), antibiotic-associated diarrhea caused by Clostridioides difficile, severe skin reactions (e.g., Stevens-Johnson Syndrome or Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis), and a specific allergic reaction called DRESS (Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms). Omeprazole may also cause lupus or worsen existing lupus, vitamin B12 deficiency, hypomagnesemia (low magnesium levels), and bone loss or fractures, particularly in older adults or those on long-term or high-dose therapy. Omeprazole may interact with other medications, including blood thinners like clopidogrel and warfarin, antidepressants like citalopram, and certain antiretroviral drugs. It can also affect the absorption of other medications due to its impact on stomach acid levels. Always inform your healthcare provider about all medications, supplements, and herbal products you are taking to avoid potential interactions. Pregnant or breastfeeding individuals should consult their healthcare provider before using omeprazole, as its effects on pregnancy and breastfed infants are not fully understood. Omeprazole should not be used by individuals allergic to its ingredients or other proton pump inhibitors. If you miss a dose of omeprazole, take it as soon as you remember unless it is almost time for your next dose. Do not take double doses. In case of an overdose, seek immediate medical attention or contact a poison control center. Omeprazole is generally safe when used as prescribed, but it is important to monitor for side effects and interactions. If you experience any unusual symptoms or reactions, contact your healthcare provider promptly.
